To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prostaglandin PGE2 induces the development of MDSCs from monocytes in vitro and that this effect is dependent on PGE2-induced COX2 expression.
prostaglandin PGE2 induces the development of myeloid derived suppressor cells (a type of immunosuppressive cell) from monocytes.
prostaglandin PGE2 induces the development of monocytic MDSC from monocytes via endogenous COX2 and the EP2/EP4 signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of MDSCs in vitro using prostaglandins.
the development of novel immunosuppressive strategies and the generation of suppressive cells for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory disorders.
the development of novel methods to control the immune response and to develop novel therapies of autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammatory diseases and transplant rejection.

the PGE2-mediated generation of MDSCs is a novel and clinically relevant method of generating suppressive cells for immunotherapy of inflammatory diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown a simple and clinically applicable method for the generation of large numbers of myeloid suppressor cells (MSCs) from human monocytes using prostaglandins (PGE2), which is an important immunomodulatory molecule and an endogenous inhibitor of the immune system.
PGE2 is an endogenous inducer of MDSCs, and this induction is driven by EP2/4-mediated signaling pathway.

prostaglandin PGE2 is a potent inducer of monocytic MDSC generation and that PGE2-induced MDSCs may be a useful therapeutic tool for immunotherapy of autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammatory conditions, and transplant rejection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

prostaglandin (PGE2) induces the development of monocytic myeloid-derived suppresor cells (MDSc) from monocytes in the presence of granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and IL-4, a process involving the induction of cyclooxygenase 2 (COX2) expression in monocytes.
PGE2, an important mediator of inflammation and a potent immunosuppressive agent, is a potent inducer of the monocytic MDSC development.
